list: The official 55 trophies, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles on 2026-11-18 (1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, 28 hidden on PlayStation). Names, descriptions and grades are exactly as PlayStation publishes them; guides are our own words.
sourcesNote: Every trophy cites Exophase for its official name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for PSN's tracked count where one exists. Specific locations and steps are best-effort guidance from the official description and are marked not yet verified in-game where they go beyond it.

trophies.guide: This is the platinum, and it needs no separate effort of its own: it pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so treat it as the finish line of the whole roadmap rather than a task to chase directly. Work through the story chapters first, then the named missions, then the stranger strands, and only then grind the activities, collectibles and cleanup trophies. Keep the checklist in this guide ticked as you go so nothing is left behind, and check the missables page before each story chapter so a single-moment trophy never has to wait for a replay.
trophies.missableNote: Cannot be missed: it unlocks automatically once the other 54 trophies are earned.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first story trophy most players earn and it cannot really be avoided: play through the introduction until the mission completes and the trophy pops at the end of it. The mission teaches the basic movement, driving and interaction controls, so take it slowly and follow the on-screen prompts and the waypoint marker rather than wandering off. If anything interrupts the mission, restart it from the pause menu and finish it in one clean run. There is nothing to collect or prepare beforehand, and no choice inside it changes the outcome.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to the opening mission Gone Fishing; replay the mission if you miss it.

trophies.guide: Chapter 1 is the first block of the story, and this trophy pops when its final mission is complete, so the route is simply to play every story mission in order until the chapter closes. Do not worry about side activities yet: the chapter missions are marked on the map, and the game will not let you skip ahead of them. Before the chapter's last mission, check the missables page for any trophy tied to a single moment inside it, and make a manual save so you can replay that mission if something goes wrong. Once the chapter-end cutscene plays, the trophy is yours.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to finishing Chapter 1; replay its missions if needed.

New areas and activities may open up as the chapter progresses, but none of them is required for this trophy, so stay on the story path if you want it quickly. As with every chapter trophy, glance at the missables page before the final mission of the chapter: any trophy tied to one moment inside it is far easier to grab on the first pass than on a replay. Finish the final mission and the trophy pops with the chapter close.

By this point the map is wide open, so it is tempting to drift into side content, but the trophy only cares about the story path: follow the mission markers and finish each one. Check the missables page before the chapter's final mission, because a trophy tied to a single moment in that mission is easiest on the first attempt, and save manually first. When the closing mission completes, the trophy unlocks and Chapter 4 begins.

The chapter is the run-up to the finale, so its missions are the longest and hardest of the story, and it pays to go in with full health, armour and ammunition, and a manual save before each big mission. Check the missables page before the chapter's final mission for any trophy tied to a single moment there. Complete the last mission of Chapter 4 and the trophy pops, leaving only the final mission between you and the gold story trophy.

trophies.guide: The gold story trophy, earned by completing the final mission after Chapter 4. This is the climax of the whole game, so go in prepared: full health and armour, your best weapons with plenty of ammunition, and a manual save made before you start it. Follow the mission objectives as they appear and do not rush the set pieces, since failing a checkpoint usually just restarts you at the last one rather than costing the trophy. Once the final cutscene plays and the credits roll, the trophy pops. After it, free roam opens up for the cleanup trophies.

There is no special condition listed in the official description, so no optional objective or collectible inside the mission is needed for the trophy itself. If the mission fails partway through, restart from the checkpoint and finish it in one clean run.

trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is one of the big named heist missions, and the trophy is earned simply by completing it. Reach it by playing the story in order, stock up on weapons, armour and ammunition beforehand, and make a manual save before starting, since heist missions tend to be long with several stages. Follow the objectives as they appear, use cover during shootouts, and keep an eye on any partner or escort objective the mission gives you. Finish the heist and escape, and the trophy unlocks at the mission's end.

Take it steadily, use the checkpoints if a section fails, and make a manual save before you begin so a failed run costs nothing. Complete the mission and the trophy is yours.

trophies.guide: The gold completion trophy: reach 100% on the game's in-game completion checklist, which counts story missions, side strands, activities, collectibles and exploration together. This is a late-game trophy by design, so do not chase it early: finish the story, then work through the roadmap stages in this guide, ticking each trophy off as you go, and use the pause menu's stats screen to see which completion categories are still short. The last few percent are almost always collectibles or activities, so the collectible and activity trophies in this guide are the practical route to it.
trophies.missableNote: Cannot be missed: 100% completion can be finished in free roam after the story.

trophies.guide: Stunts are the jumps, near misses, drifts and airtime moments the game counts as you drive, ride and fly around Leonida, and PSN tracks them up to 250. The practical way is to drive fast and recklessly on purpose during normal play: hit jump ramps and hills at speed, drift corners, thread between traffic for near misses, and catch air off ramps and ridges. It is a long grind, so let it build naturally through the story and finish the remainder in free roam with a fast car and a favourite ramp.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: stunts can be done any time in free roam.

Watch for the on-screen stunt notifications as you drive.

In free roam, repeat a good ramp run until you reach 250.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Leonida offers nine activity types, and this trophy asks you to try each one once — not to master any of them. The official description does not name the nine, so work through the activity icons on the map one by one: fishing, the shooting range, drone races, races, arcade games, bowling and the other open-world activities the game marks for you. Trying one means starting it and taking part, so a single attempt at each is enough even if you lose. Tick each off in your notes here as you go, and the trophy pops when the ninth type is sampled. Specific activity names beyond the ones this guide names are best-effort, not yet verified in-game.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: activities stay open in free roam after the story.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The shooting range holds 42 challenges, and this silver trophy needs a gold medal in every one of them — the hardest pure-skill trophy in the set. Go to a shooting range, pick a challenge, and learn its target layout and par time or score before chasing gold: steady aim beats fast spray, and Combat Focus helps you line up shots. Work through the challenges one weapon class at a time, replaying any that fall short, and use the range's own feedback to see which targets cost you time. Expect this to take several sessions, so leave it for the cleanup stage and treat it as a skill grind, not a story task.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: the shooting range stays open in free roam.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun runs drone races at 14 locations across Leonida, and this trophy needs a win at each one. Find a Top Fun drone-race marker on the map, start the race, and fly the course through its checkpoints as cleanly as you can: smooth lines and gentle corrections beat aggressive diving, and learning a course once before racing it hard saves crashes. Win the race at that location, then move to the next marker until all 14 are won. The trophy pops on the fourteenth win. If a course keeps beating you, replay it to learn the turns, then race it again. Exact course layouts are not yet verified in-game.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: drone races stay open in free roam.

trophies.guide: This trophy counts distinct races won, so winning the same race twenty times does not count: you need 20 different race events across Leonida. Open the map and work through the race markers one by one, picking a fast, well-handling vehicle and learning each route's corners before you push hard. Shorter races are the efficient picks early on, and a clean start matters more than top speed on most courses. Keep a note of which races you have already won so you never repeat one by mistake, and the trophy pops on your twentieth different win.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: races stay open in free roam.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is a fishing rival, and this trophy is earned by beating him in a fishing challenge. Go fishing where the challenge is offered, start the challenge against Cal, and fish the way the game teaches: cast to where the fish are, watch the line tension, and reel steadily without snapping it. Bigger or more numerous catches than Cal's score wins the challenge, so take your time on each cast rather than rushing. If Cal wins the first attempt, simply challenge him again — the trophy only needs one win, and the challenge stays available. Exact fishing mechanics are best-effort, not yet verified in-game.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: the fishing challenge can be retried.

trophies.guide: Leonida's arcades hold playable arcade games, and this trophy needs you to complete one of them — finish a full game, not just start it. Find an arcade, walk up to a machine, and play the game through to its end, whether that means clearing its levels, reaching its goal, or surviving to its conclusion. Pick the simplest-looking machine first if you are chasing the trophy quickly, and do not worry about a high score: completion is the requirement, not mastery. Once the game's end screen shows, the trophy pops. Which machines count is best-effort, not yet verified in-game.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.

Each strand is usually short — a drive, a favour, or a small task — and counts once its final mission is done. Eight strands is the target, so keep count in your notes here and the trophy pops when the eighth strand closes. Exact stranger names and locations are not yet verified in-game.

trophies.guide: There are 18 meditation spots scattered across Leonida, and this trophy needs you to meditate at every one of them. Find a spot — usually a scenic viewpoint or quiet place marked on the map or found while exploring — stand in it and use the meditate prompt, then wait for the moment to register before moving on. Work through the map region by region so you do not lose track, and note each spot you have done in the notes field here. The trophy pops at the eighteenth spot. trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret wants a unique animal hunted, and this trophy is earned by tracking it down and taking it. Find Bret's hunting mission or marker, then follow the hunt: look for tracks, listen for the animal's sounds, and approach slowly so it does not bolt before you are in range. Use a scoped or accurate weapon for a clean shot, and take the shot only when you are steady, since a unique animal may not give you a second chance in the same attempt. If the hunt fails, retry it from Bret's marker. The animal's species and location are not yet verified in-game.

trophies.guide: Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida in sets, and this silver trophy needs three full sets completed. Pick up every card you find while exploring — they are usually in distinctive spots, on shelves, in shops and at landmarks — and check your collection screen to see which sets are close to complete. A set counts only when every card in it is found, so a nearly finished set is worth a focused sweep of the area its remaining cards hide in. Three completed sets earns the trophy. Exact card locations are not yet verified in-game, so explore thoroughly and use the collection screen as your checklist.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: cards stay collectible in free roam.

trophies.guide: WAiNK It is a photo or check-in style activity at 100 locations across Leonida, and this silver trophy needs all one hundred. The practical approach is to treat it as an exploration grind: travel region by region, use the WAiNK prompt at each marked location, and let the counter climb. Check PSN's tracked count as you go so you know how far along you are, and do not waste time revisiting a location you have already done — the game should mark it as visited. One hundred is a lot, so spread it across your free-roam cleanup rather than trying to finish it in one session. Exact location list is not yet verified in-game.
